content: Hi all, I’m working on a research project related to Lean and operating systems. In short, I am trying to use Lean (within the programming language context) to implement part of an operating system. The key challenge here is when compiling Lean to C, the generated code must be “bare-bones” and not rely on any system calls or other user space features. Question 1, do projects exist that do this in any capacity that can serve as a reference for this project? Question 2, at a higher level, is there a way to enforce that Lean generates code without standard library functionality?

Pretty unlikely. There are a few projects that have done Haskell and osdev, see https://wiki.osdev.org/Haskell, so you might want to take a look at those. Personally, I think using rust for these things is way more natural and convenient. There you get away with using a tiny bit of assembly and then can do everything in rust. For Lean there is no support to opt out of things like memory allocation, so you need to setup a run time in a different language first.
